# Paste-ready fixes: Android

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate.py. Don't edit by hand. -->

These snippets are released under MIT-0: use them in any app, no attribution needed. Adapt names to the project, keep the logic.

## AND-001: Cleartext (plain HTTP) traffic is allowed

Remove `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"` from the base config (and `android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"` from the manifest). If one host really needs HTTP, allow only that host in a `<domain-config>`.

```xml
<network-security-config>
    <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false" />
    <!-- Only if a host truly needs HTTP: -->
    <!-- <domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"><domain>legacy.example.com</domain></domain-config> -->
</network-security-config>
```

Verify: Build a release APK, open an `http://` URL your app uses, and confirm the request fails with a cleartext error.

Book: [§7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

## AND-002: Release build is debuggable

Remove `android:debuggable="true"` from the main manifest and set `isDebuggable = false` (Groovy: `debuggable false`) in the `release` build type. Let the `debug` build type stay debuggable.

```kotlin
// app/build.gradle.kts
android {
    buildTypes {
        debug {
            isDebuggable = true
        }
        release {
            isDebuggable = false
            isMinifyEnabled = true
            isShrinkResources = true
            proguardFiles(
                getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android-optimize.txt"),
                "proguard-rules.pro"
            )
        }
    }
}
```

Verify: Build the release APK (or extract one from the bundle with bundletool) and run `aapt2 dump badging app-release.apk | grep application-debuggable`. It should print nothing.

Book: [§14.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#141-the-cheap-things-which-you-should-simply-do)

## AND-003: User-installed CAs are trusted in release

Remove `<certificates src="user"/>` from `base-config` and `domain-config`. If you need a proxy while developing, put it inside `<debug-overrides>`, which Android uses only in debuggable builds.

```xml
<network-security-config>
    <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <trust-anchors>
            <certificates src="system" />
        </trust-anchors>
    </base-config>
    <!-- Only honored when android:debuggable="true". Lets you proxy debug builds. -->
    <debug-overrides>
        <trust-anchors>
            <certificates src="user" />
        </trust-anchors>
    </debug-overrides>
</network-security-config>
```

Verify: Install a proxy CA on a test phone, run the release build through the proxy, and confirm HTTPS requests fail.

Book: [§7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

## AND-004: WebView ignores TLS certificate errors

Call `handler.cancel()` in `onReceivedSslError` and never `handler.proceed()`. Fix the certificate on the server instead.

```kotlin
override fun onReceivedSslError(
    view: WebView, handler: SslErrorHandler, error: SslError
) {
    handler.cancel()                   // NEVER handler.proceed()
}
```

Verify: Point the WebView at a site with a bad certificate (for example through a proxy without its CA installed) and confirm the page doesn't load.

Book: [§16.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#164-loading-untrusted-content)

## AND-005: TrustManager or HostnameVerifier accepts everything

Delete the custom TrustManager and HostnameVerifier and use the platform defaults. If you need pinning, add a `<pin-set>` or OkHttp `CertificatePinner`, which run on top of normal validation.

```kotlin
// Delete .sslSocketFactory(..., trustAllManager) and .hostnameVerifier { _, _ -> true }.
// The default client validates the chain and the host name.
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .connectionSpecs(listOf(ConnectionSpec.MODERN_TLS))
    // High-risk apps only: pins run on top of normal validation (§8.8).
    // .certificatePinner(CertificatePinner.Builder().add("api.example.com", "sha256/...").build())
    .build()
```

Verify: Send the app's traffic through a proxy whose CA the phone doesn't trust and confirm every request fails.

Book: [§7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

## AND-006: OkHttp or SSLContext allows old TLS or plain HTTP

Use `ConnectionSpec.MODERN_TLS` (TLS 1.3 and 1.2 only) and leave `ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT` out of the list. Request `SSLContext.getInstance("TLS")`, not `SSL` or `TLSv1`.

```kotlin
// OkHttp 5.x. MODERN_TLS already offers TLS 1.3 and 1.2 only.
// Leaving ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT out of the list makes every http:// URL fail.
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .connectionSpecs(listOf(ConnectionSpec.MODERN_TLS))
    .build()
```

Verify: Check that an `http://` URL fails and that a server limited to TLS 1.1 is refused.

Book: [§7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

## AND-007: No certificate pinning (needed for high-risk apps)

Pin the SPKI of your CA's intermediate in `network_security_config.xml`, with a backup pin at a second CA and an expiration date. Write a rotation runbook before you ship it. Pin only if you can also run failure alerts, CT monitoring, and a protected kill switch (§8.7); if not, don't pin and rely on strict TLS plus CT (§8.9).

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!-- res/xml/network_security_config.xml -->
<network-security-config>
    <domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <domain includeSubdomains="true">api.example.com</domain>
        <!-- base64 SHA-256 of the SPKI, not of the whole certificate -->
        <pin-set expiration="2027-12-31">
            <!-- Primary: your CA's intermediate -->
            <pin digest="SHA-256">YLh1dUR9y6Kja30RrAn7JKnbQG/uEtLMkBgFF2Fuihg=</pin>
            <!-- Backup: an intermediate at a second CA, or a spare key you hold -->
            <pin digest="SHA-256">Vjs8r4z+80wjNcr1YKepWQboSIRi63WsWXhIMN+eWys=</pin>
        </pin-set>
    </domain-config>
</network-security-config>
<!-- The pin values are placeholders: generate your own (§8.10). -->
```

Verify: Configure a wrong pin on a test build and confirm connections fail with a pin error. Then restore the real pins.

Book: [§8.8](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#88-the-decision-by-application-type)

## AND-008: Pin set has no backup pin or no expiration date

Add a second pin for an intermediate at another CA (or a spare key you hold), and set `expiration` a little past the longest time you support a build. Set a reminder well before that date.

```xml
<pin-set expiration="2027-12-31">
    <!-- Primary: your CA's intermediate -->
    <pin digest="SHA-256">YLh1dUR9y6Kja30RrAn7JKnbQG/uEtLMkBgFF2Fuihg=</pin>
    <!-- Backup: an intermediate at a second CA, or a spare key you hold -->
    <pin digest="SHA-256">Vjs8r4z+80wjNcr1YKepWQboSIRi63WsWXhIMN+eWys=</pin>
</pin-set>
```

Verify: Read `network_security_config.xml` in the release APK and confirm each `<pin-set>` has two or more pins and a future `expiration`.

Book: [§8.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#86-where-the-pins-live-static-dynamic-and-hybrid)

## AND-009: Pinning or certificate trust depends on a BuildConfig flag

Configure pinning and trust the same way in every build. Put debug-only trust in `src/debug/` (for example a `network_security_config.xml` with `<debug-overrides>`) so the code doesn't exist in release.

```xml
<!-- app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml: exists only in debug builds -->
<network-security-config>
    <debug-overrides>
        <trust-anchors>
            <certificates src="user" />
        </trust-anchors>
    </debug-overrides>
</network-security-config>
```

Verify: Decompile the release APK and confirm the relaxed trust path isn't there.

Book: [§15.8](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#158-build-configuration-in-code)

## AND-010: WebView can read local files

Remove `allowFileAccess = true` and never enable `allowFileAccessFromFileURLs` or `allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs`. Serve bundled HTML with `WebViewAssetLoader` over `https://appassets.androidplatform.net/`.

```kotlin
webView.settings.apply {
    javaScriptEnabled = false            // turn on only if the page needs it
    allowFileAccess = false              // default false only when targeting API 30+
    allowContentAccess = false           // defaults to true on every version
    // allowFileAccessFromFileURLs / allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs are deprecated
    // and already false when targeting API 16+. Never set them to true.
}
```

Verify: Load a test page that tries to fetch a `file:///data/data/<package>/` URL and confirm it's blocked.

Book: [§16.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#163-file-access-the-setting-nobody-remembers-changing)

## AND-012: JavaScript bridge is reachable from every frame

Use `WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener` with an allowlist of origins, and validate every message. If you must keep `addJavascriptInterface`, expose one narrow method and treat its input as untrusted.

```kotlin
if (WebViewFeature.isFeatureSupported(WebViewFeature.WEB_MESSAGE_LISTENER)) {
    WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener(
        webView,
        "AppBridge",                                   // window.AppBridge in the page
        setOf("https://app.example.com"),              // the platform enforces this
    ) { _, message, sourceOrigin, isMainFrame, replyProxy ->
        if (!isMainFrame || sourceOrigin.host != "app.example.com") return@addWebMessageListener
        val code = message.data ?: return@addWebMessageListener
        if (!Regex("^[A-Z0-9]{8}$").matches(code)) return@addWebMessageListener
        redeemVoucher(code)                            // the server authorizes; the bridge does not
        replyProxy.postMessage("received")
    }
}
```

Verify: Load a page with a third-party iframe and confirm the iframe can't reach the bridge.

Book: [§16.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#162-the-javascript-bridge-and-why-its-the-sharpest-edge)

## AND-013: WebView debugging is on in release

Tie debugging to the build type: `WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(debuggable)`, where `debuggable` comes from `FLAG_DEBUGGABLE`. Never pass a plain `true`.

```kotlin
import android.content.pm.ApplicationInfo
import android.webkit.WebView

// Debugging follows the build type. Never call this with `true` unconditionally.
val debuggable = (applicationInfo.flags and ApplicationInfo.FLAG_DEBUGGABLE) != 0
WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(debuggable)
```

Verify: Install the release build, open `chrome://inspect` on a computer, and confirm the app's WebViews aren't listed.

Book: [§16.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#166-cleanup-and-hygiene)

## AND-014: WebView loads a URL from an intent or deep link

Parse the URL with `Uri.parse`, require `https`, and compare the parsed host with an exact allowlist before calling `loadUrl`. Check again in `shouldOverrideUrlLoading`.

```kotlin
private val allowedHosts = setOf("app.example.com", "help.example.com")

// Exact host match on the parsed URL, https only. NOT `url.contains("example.com")`.
fun isAllowed(uri: Uri): Boolean =
    uri.scheme == "https" && uri.host?.lowercase() in allowedHosts

// shouldOverrideUrlLoading does not see this call, so check it here too.
fun openInWebView(target: Uri) {
    if (isAllowed(target)) webView.loadUrl(target.toString())
}
```

Verify: Send the app a link that carries `https://evil.example/` as the URL parameter and confirm the WebView refuses it.

Book: [§16.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#164-loading-untrusted-content)

## AND-015: Exported component has no permission

Set `android:exported="false"` unless other apps must reach the component. If they must, require a permission with `android:protectionLevel="signature"` and validate every input.

```xml
<activity android:name=".InternalActivity" android:exported="false" />

<!-- Shared only with your own apps: same signing key required -->
<permission android:name="com.example.permission.SYNC"
    android:protectionLevel="signature" />
<service android:name=".SyncService"
    android:exported="true"
    android:permission="com.example.permission.SYNC" />
```

Verify: Run `adb shell am start -n <package>/<component>` (or `am startservice`, `am broadcast`) from a shell and confirm it's refused.

Book: [§17.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#171-android-app-components-and-the-word-exported)

## AND-016: FileProvider shares too much of the filesystem

Scope each entry in `file_paths.xml` to the narrowest folder that works, such as `<cache-path name="shared_exports" path="exports/" />`. Remove `<root-path>`. Grant read, not write, unless the recipient must write.

```xml
<!-- res/xml/file_paths.xml -->
<paths>
    <cache-path name="shared_exports" path="exports/" />
    <!-- Never: <root-path name="root" path="" />  or  path="." -->
</paths>
```

Verify: Ask the provider for a URI that points at `../databases/` and confirm it fails.

Book: [§17.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#174-content-providers)

## AND-017: App starts an Intent it received from another app

Don't forward nested Intents. If you must, run them through AndroidX `IntentSanitizer`, allowing only the component and extras you expect.

```kotlin
val nested = IntentCompat.getParcelableExtra(intent, "next", Intent::class.java) ?: return

// Keep only what you expect. Flags you did not allow, including FLAG_GRANT_*, are dropped.
val safe = IntentSanitizer.Builder()
    .allowComponent(ComponentName(this, ReceiptActivity::class.java))
    .allowExtra("receipt_id", String::class.java)
    .build()
    .sanitizeByFiltering(nested)

startActivity(safe)
```

Verify: From a test app, send an Intent whose extra points at one of your non-exported activities and confirm it doesn't open.

Book: [§17.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#172-intents-explicit-versus-implicit)

## AND-018: Mutable PendingIntent

Use `PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE` with an explicit Intent. Keep `FLAG_MUTABLE` only where you need it, such as inline replies, and make the base Intent explicit there.

```kotlin
val intent = Intent(context, ResultReceiverActivity::class.java)   // explicit
val pendingIntent = PendingIntent.getActivity(
    context, 0, intent,
    PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE or PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT
)
```

Verify: Check each place that creates a `PendingIntent` and confirm it's immutable or has an explicit component.

Book: [§17.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#173-pendingintent-the-one-that-looks-harmless)

## AND-019: App Link is not verified

Add `android:autoVerify="true"` to the `https` intent filter and host `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` with your app signing certificate fingerprint.

```xml
<activity android:name=".TransferActivity" android:exported="true">
    <intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
        <data android:scheme="https" android:host="app.example.com" android:pathPrefix="/transfer" />
    </intent-filter>
</activity>
```

Verify: Run `adb shell pm get-app-links <package>` on a Play install and confirm each domain shows `verified`.

Book: [§17.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#175-deep-links-and-the-verification-that-makes-them-safe)

## AND-020: SQL query built by joining strings

Use `?` placeholders and pass values as `selectionArgs`, or Room `@Query` with bound parameters. Allowlist column names and sort orders.

```kotlin
// Bound values, never string concatenation.
db.rawQuery("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = ?", arrayOf(currentUserId))
```

Verify: Pass `' OR '1'='1` into the code path and confirm it's treated as plain text.

Book: [§19.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#193-injection-the-shape-of-the-bug)

## AND-021: Backup is on with no exclusion rules

Add `android:dataExtractionRules` (Android 12+) and `android:fullBackupContent` (Android 11 and lower) that exclude secrets and their keysets, in both `<cloud-backup>` and `<device-transfer>`.

```xml
<!-- AndroidManifest.xml -->
<application
    android:allowBackup="true"
    android:dataExtractionRules="@xml/data_extraction_rules"
    android:fullBackupContent="@xml/backup_rules">
</application>

<!-- res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml: Android 12+ when targeting API 31+ -->
<data-extraction-rules>
    <cloud-backup disableIfNoEncryptionCapabilities="true">
        <exclude domain="file" path="datastore/session.enc" />
        <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="tink_keysets.xml" />
    </cloud-backup>
    <device-transfer>
        <exclude domain="file" path="datastore/session.enc" />
        <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="tink_keysets.xml" />
    </device-transfer>
</data-extraction-rules>

<!-- res/xml/backup_rules.xml: Android 11 and lower -->
<full-backup-content>
    <exclude domain="file" path="datastore/session.enc" />
    <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="tink_keysets.xml" />
</full-backup-content>
```

Verify: Run `adb shell bmgr backupnow <package>` over an encrypted local transport, reinstall, and confirm the excluded files are gone after the restore.

Book: [§6.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#65-the-leaks-that-are-not-about-encryption)

## AND-022: Deprecated EncryptedSharedPreferences (Jetpack Security)

If the stored values aren't secrets (flags, UI state), move them to plain DataStore or SharedPreferences: the sandbox already protects them (§6.4). For tokens and credentials, use DataStore, Tink, and an Android Keystore master key (`androidx.datastore:datastore-tink`). Migrate with `SharedPreferencesMigration`, then delete the old file and Keystore alias.

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    implementation("androidx.datastore:datastore:1.3.0-rc01")
    implementation("androidx.datastore:datastore-tink:1.3.0-rc01")  // pre-release: pin and test
    implementation("com.google.crypto.tink:tink-android:1.24.0")
}
```

Verify: Confirm the dependency is gone from the build and that `files/datastore/` holds only binary ciphertext.

Book: [§6.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#61-encryptedsharedpreferences-is-dead)

## AND-023: End-of-life SQLCipher package

Switch to `net.zetetic:sqlcipher-android` (package `net.zetetic.database.sqlcipher`). Use `SupportOpenHelperFactory` with Room 2 or `SQLCipherDriver` with Room 3.

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts:
//   implementation("net.zetetic:sqlcipher-android:4.19.1@aar")
//   implementation("androidx.sqlite:sqlite:<the version SQLCipher's README names>")

import net.zetetic.database.sqlcipher.driver.SQLCipherDriver

fun buildDatabase(context: Context, passphrase: ByteArray): AppDatabase {
    System.loadLibrary("sqlcipher")                  // once, before first use
    return Room.databaseBuilder(
            context, AppDatabase::class.java, context.getDatabasePath("app.db").absolutePath
        )
        .setDriver(SQLCipherDriver(passphrase, null, null))
        .build()
}
```

Verify: Confirm the old coordinates and `net.sqlcipher` imports are gone, then open an existing database to check the migration.

Book: [§6.7](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#67-encrypting-a-local-database)

## AND-024: Tink may silently store its keyset in plain text

After `build()`, check `manager.isUsingKeystore` and record the result (for example in security telemetry), so you know when the fallback happens.

```kotlin
val manager = AndroidKeysetManager.Builder()
    .withSharedPref(context, "session_keyset", "tink_keysets")
    .withKeyTemplate(KeyTemplate.createFrom(PredefinedAeadParameters.AES256_GCM))
    .withMasterKeyUri("android-keystore://session_master_key")
    .build()
if (!manager.isUsingKeystore) {
    // Tink fell back to a cleartext keyset. Record it; do not pretend.
    SecurityTelemetry.record("tink_keystore_unavailable")
}
```

Verify: Log `isUsingKeystore` in a debug build on your test devices and confirm it's `true` where you expect hardware backing.

Book: [§6.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#63-what-to-use-instead)

## AND-025: Biometric prompt is not tied to a key

Pass a `CryptoObject` wrapping a Keystore key created with `setUserAuthenticationRequired(true)`, and do the protected work (sign or decrypt) with `result.cryptoObject` in the success callback.

```kotlin
val callback = object : BiometricPrompt.AuthenticationCallback() {
    override fun onAuthenticationSucceeded(result: BiometricPrompt.AuthenticationResult) {
        // Use the unlocked object. Never just note that authentication "succeeded".
        val unlocked = result.cryptoObject?.signature ?: return onFailed()
        unlocked.update(challengeAndTransfer)
        onSigned(unlocked.sign())
    }
}

BiometricPrompt(activity, ContextCompat.getMainExecutor(activity), callback)
    .authenticate(promptInfo, BiometricPrompt.CryptoObject(signature))
```

Verify: Run a biometric-bypass Frida script against a debug build and confirm the protected action still fails.

Book: [§11.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#111-decorative-versus-real)

## AND-026: Biometric key survives a new fingerprint or face

Keep `setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment(true)` (the default), use `setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, KeyProperties.AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG)`, and don't add `AUTH_DEVICE_CREDENTIAL` or a validity window to the key.

```kotlin
val spec = KeyGenParameterSpec.Builder(TRANSFER_KEY_ALIAS, KeyProperties.PURPOSE_SIGN)
    .setAlgorithmParameterSpec(ECGenParameterSpec("secp256r1"))
    .setDigests(KeyProperties.DIGEST_SHA256)
    .setUserAuthenticationRequired(true)
    .apply {
        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.N) {
            setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment(true)     // the default for this shape; say it anyway
        }
        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.R) {
            // 0 = authenticate for every use. Biometric only: no device-credential fallback.
            setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, KeyProperties.AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG)
        }
    }
    .build()
```

Verify: Add a new fingerprint on a test phone and confirm using the key throws `KeyPermanentlyInvalidatedException`.

Book: [§11.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#113-the-enrollment-problem-nobody-thinks-about)

## AND-027: R8 is off in the release build

Set `isMinifyEnabled = true` and `isShrinkResources = true` in the `release` build type, with `proguard-android-optimize.txt`. Keep only the keep rules reflection needs.

```kotlin
// app/build.gradle.kts
android {
    buildTypes {
        release {
            isMinifyEnabled = true
            isShrinkResources = true
            proguardFiles(
                getDefaultProguardFile("proguard-android-optimize.txt"),
                "proguard-rules.pro"
            )
        }
    }
}
```

Verify: Decompile the release APK with jadx and confirm your class names are shortened.

Book: [§14.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#141-the-cheap-things-which-you-should-simply-do)

Raise `targetSdk` to 36 or later, then test the behavior changes for each version you skipped.

```kotlin
android {
    defaultConfig {
        targetSdk = 36
    }
}
```

Verify: Run `aapt2 dump badging app-release.apk | grep targetSdkVersion` and confirm it shows 36 or more.

Book: [§19.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#196-free-compiler-protections-and-platform-currency)

## AND-029: minSdk is below 24

Raise `minSdk` to at least 24. Android ignores the network security config below API 24, so it can't protect those devices. If you must support them, use a TrustManager that trusts only system CAs (or OkHttp `CertificatePinner` in a high-risk app), or accept the risk for those users.

```kotlin
android {
    defaultConfig {
        minSdk = 24
    }
}
```

Verify: Run `aapt2 dump badging app-release.apk | grep sdkVersion` and confirm it shows 24 or more.

Book: [§19.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#196-free-compiler-protections-and-platform-currency)

## AND-030: HTTP bodies are logged in every build

Use `Level.BODY` only when `BuildConfig.DEBUG` is true and `Level.NONE` otherwise, or add the interceptor only in debug builds.

```kotlin
val logging = HttpLoggingInterceptor().apply {
    level = if (BuildConfig.DEBUG) HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.BODY
            else HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.NONE
}
```

Verify: Run the release build, sign in, and watch `adb logcat --pid=$(adb shell pidof -s <package>)`. No request bodies or tokens should appear.

Book: [§6.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#65-the-leaks-that-are-not-about-encryption)

## AND-032: Java deserialization with ObjectInputStream

Parse into declared types instead: JSON with `kotlinx.serialization`, or Protocol Buffers. For intent extras, use the typed `IntentCompat.getParcelableExtra(intent, name, Class)`.

```kotlin
// Only a ShareRequest can come out. Anything else returns null.
val request: ShareRequest? =
    IntentCompat.getParcelableExtra(intent, "request", ShareRequest::class.java)
```

Verify: Feed the decoder a payload that names a class you didn't expect and confirm it's rejected.

Book: [§19.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#194-deserialization)

## AND-034: Token or password stored in plain SharedPreferences or DataStore

Keep short-lived tokens in memory. Encrypt long-lived tokens before storing them, with a key held in the Android Keystore: for example Tink's AEAD with an `AndroidKeysetManager` master key, checking `isUsingKeystore()`. Keep only non-secret settings in plain preferences.

```kotlin
import com.google.crypto.tink.Aead

// `aead` comes from Tink's AndroidKeysetManager with a Keystore master key (see AND-024).
class TokenStore(private val prefs: android.content.SharedPreferences, private val aead: Aead) {
    fun save(token: String) {
        val sealed = aead.encrypt(token.toByteArray(), "refresh_token".toByteArray())
        prefs.edit().putString("refresh_token", android.util.Base64.encodeToString(sealed, android.util.Base64.NO_WRAP)).apply()
    }

    fun load(): String? = prefs.getString("refresh_token", null)?.let {
        String(aead.decrypt(android.util.Base64.decode(it, android.util.Base64.NO_WRAP), "refresh_token".toByteArray()))
    }
}
```

Verify: Sign in on an emulator, then run `adb shell run-as <package> ls -R shared_prefs files/datastore` and print each file with `cat`. Confirm no token or password appears in readable form.

Book: [§6.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#64-the-uncomfortable-question-nobody-asked)

## XPL-004: AES in ECB mode, or with no mode named

Use AES-GCM (`AES/GCM/NoPadding`) with a Keystore key, or Tink's AEAD, or CryptoKit's `AES.GCM` on iOS. Re-encrypt existing data under the new scheme.

```kotlin
import javax.crypto.Cipher
import javax.crypto.SecretKey
import javax.crypto.spec.GCMParameterSpec

private const val IV_BYTES = 12
private const val TAG_BITS = 128

fun encrypt(plaintext: ByteArray, key: SecretKey, aad: ByteArray): ByteArray {
    val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")
    cipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, key)          // the Keystore generates the IV; do not supply one
    cipher.updateAAD(aad)                          // e.g. "refresh_token", binds purpose to ciphertext
    val ciphertext = cipher.doFinal(plaintext)
    return cipher.iv + ciphertext                  // store the IV alongside; it is not secret
}

fun decrypt(stored: ByteArray, key: SecretKey, aad: ByteArray): ByteArray {
    val iv = stored.copyOfRange(0, IV_BYTES)
    val ciphertext = stored.copyOfRange(IV_BYTES, stored.size)
    val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")
    cipher.init(Cipher.DECRYPT_MODE, key, GCMParameterSpec(TAG_BITS, iv))
    cipher.updateAAD(aad)
    return cipher.doFinal(ciphertext)              // throws AEADBadTagException if tampered
}
```

Verify: Search for `AES/ECB`, `"AES"`, and `kCCOptionECBMode`; every remaining hit should be gone or explained in a comment.

Book: [Chapter 0.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-02-cryptography-you-actually-need)

## XPL-005: AES-CBC needs a separate MAC to detect tampering

Prefer AES-GCM. If you must keep CBC, compute an HMAC-SHA-256 over the IV and the ciphertext with a separate key, and check it in constant time before decrypting.

```kotlin
import javax.crypto.Cipher
import javax.crypto.SecretKey
import javax.crypto.spec.GCMParameterSpec

private const val IV_BYTES = 12
private const val TAG_BITS = 128

fun encrypt(plaintext: ByteArray, key: SecretKey, aad: ByteArray): ByteArray {
    val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")
    cipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, key)          // the Keystore generates the IV; do not supply one
    cipher.updateAAD(aad)                          // e.g. "refresh_token", binds purpose to ciphertext
    val ciphertext = cipher.doFinal(plaintext)
    return cipher.iv + ciphertext                  // store the IV alongside; it is not secret
}

fun decrypt(stored: ByteArray, key: SecretKey, aad: ByteArray): ByteArray {
    val iv = stored.copyOfRange(0, IV_BYTES)
    val ciphertext = stored.copyOfRange(IV_BYTES, stored.size)
    val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")
    cipher.init(Cipher.DECRYPT_MODE, key, GCMParameterSpec(TAG_BITS, iv))
    cipher.updateAAD(aad)
    return cipher.doFinal(ciphertext)              // throws AEADBadTagException if tampered
}
```

Verify: For each hit, confirm a MAC over IV plus ciphertext is checked before decryption, or that the code moved to GCM.

Book: [Chapter 0.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-02-cryptography-you-actually-need)

## XPL-006: Fixed IV or nonce

Don't supply an IV. Let the Keystore, Tink, or CryptoKit generate a random 12-byte nonce for each encryption, and store it next to the ciphertext.

```kotlin
import javax.crypto.Cipher
import javax.crypto.SecretKey
import javax.crypto.spec.GCMParameterSpec

private const val IV_BYTES = 12
private const val TAG_BITS = 128

fun encrypt(plaintext: ByteArray, key: SecretKey, aad: ByteArray): ByteArray {
    val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")
    cipher.init(Cipher.ENCRYPT_MODE, key)          // the Keystore generates the IV; do not supply one
    cipher.updateAAD(aad)                          // e.g. "refresh_token", binds purpose to ciphertext
    val ciphertext = cipher.doFinal(plaintext)
    return cipher.iv + ciphertext                  // store the IV alongside; it is not secret
}

fun decrypt(stored: ByteArray, key: SecretKey, aad: ByteArray): ByteArray {
    val iv = stored.copyOfRange(0, IV_BYTES)
    val ciphertext = stored.copyOfRange(IV_BYTES, stored.size)
    val cipher = Cipher.getInstance("AES/GCM/NoPadding")
    cipher.init(Cipher.DECRYPT_MODE, key, GCMParameterSpec(TAG_BITS, iv))
    cipher.updateAAD(aad)
    return cipher.doFinal(ciphertext)              // throws AEADBadTagException if tampered
}
```

Verify: For each encryption call, confirm the IV comes from `cipher.iv` after `init`, or from a secure random source, never from a constant.

Book: [Chapter 0.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-02-cryptography-you-actually-need)

## XPL-007: MD5 or SHA-1 used (fine only as a non-security checksum)

Use SHA-256 or stronger. If the hash is only a non-security checksum, such as detecting a corrupted download, add a comment saying so.

```kotlin
val digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")
    .digest(verifier.toByteArray(Charsets.US_ASCII))

// Swift (CryptoKit)
// Data(SHA256.hash(data: Data(verifier.utf8)))
```

Verify: For each hit, confirm it uses SHA-256 or is commented as a non-security checksum.

Book: [Chapter 0.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-02-cryptography-you-actually-need)

## XPL-008: Non-cryptographic or seeded random number generator

For keys, nonces, salts, and tokens, use `SecureRandom()` with the default constructor on Android and `SecRandomCopyBytes` on iOS, and never seed them. Other uses, such as shuffling a list for display, are fine.

```kotlin
val bytes = ByteArray(32)
SecureRandom().nextBytes(bytes) // never java.util.Random or kotlin.random.Random

// Swift
// var bytes = [UInt8](repeating: 0, count: 32)
// let status = SecRandomCopyBytes(kSecRandomDefault, bytes.count, &bytes)
// guard status == errSecSuccess else { throw PKCEError.randomGenerationFailed(status) }
```

Verify: For each hit, confirm the value doesn't protect anything, or that it now comes from `SecureRandom` or `SecRandomCopyBytes`.

Book: [Chapter 0.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-02-cryptography-you-actually-need)

## XPL-010: Token, password, or secret written to the log

Remove the value from the message. Plant a release logging tree that drops everything below error, and strip `Log.v/d/i` with R8's `-assumenosideeffects`. On iOS, remove debug logging from release builds; where a log line stays, use `Logger` and leave dynamic values at the default `.private` privacy, never `privacy: .public` for a token.

```kotlin
// Application.onCreate
if (BuildConfig.DEBUG) {
    Timber.plant(Timber.DebugTree())
} else {
    Timber.plant(object : Timber.Tree() {
        override fun log(priority: Int, tag: String?, message: String, t: Throwable?) {
            if (priority >= Log.ERROR) crashReporter.log(message)   // no verbose/debug/info
        }
    })
}
```

Verify: Install a release build, sign in, and watch `adb logcat` (or Console.app on iOS): no token or password should appear.

Book: [§6.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#65-the-leaks-that-are-not-about-encryption)

## XPL-011: Encryption key is hardcoded in the app

Generate the key on the device inside the Android Keystore or the iOS Keychain or Secure Enclave, and never export it. Tink with a Keystore-protected keyset does this for you. If a server must decrypt, wrap a random per-session key with the server's public key instead of sharing one symmetric key.

```kotlin
import android.security.keystore.KeyGenParameterSpec
import android.security.keystore.KeyProperties
import java.security.KeyStore
import javax.crypto.KeyGenerator
import javax.crypto.SecretKey

private const val KEY_ALIAS = "app_data_key"

// The key is created inside the Keystore and its bytes never leave it.
fun dataKey(): SecretKey {
    val keyStore = KeyStore.getInstance("AndroidKeyStore").apply { load(null) }
    (keyStore.getKey(KEY_ALIAS, null) as? SecretKey)?.let { return it }
    val generator = KeyGenerator.getInstance(KeyProperties.KEY_ALGORITHM_AES, "AndroidKeyStore")
    generator.init(
        KeyGenParameterSpec.Builder(KEY_ALIAS, KeyProperties.PURPOSE_ENCRYPT or KeyProperties.PURPOSE_DECRYPT)
            .setBlockModes(KeyProperties.BLOCK_MODE_GCM)
            .setEncryptionPaddings(KeyProperties.ENCRYPTION_PADDING_NONE)
            .setKeySize(256)
            .build(),
    )
    return generator.generateKey()
}
```

Verify: For every `SecretKeySpec(`, `SymmetricKey(data:`, and `Key.from…(` call, confirm the key bytes come from the Keystore, the Keychain, Tink, or a secure random source, never from a string or byte literal.

Book: [Chapter 0.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-02-cryptography-you-actually-need)
